```{r setup, include=FALSE}

```

H1: Points allocated to a partner's physical attractiveness differ by sex at birth.

H2: Confidence in finding a new partner is associated with relationship commitment.

## 1. Load the package and data

```{r load, message=FALSE}
#load the codebook package
library(codebook)

#load data/raw/data_doctored.csv
raw<-read.csv("Data/Raw Data/data_doctored.csv")

#check row and column counts, and inspect the first few rows
dim(raw)
str(raw)


#make data with ID, sex at birth, relationship status, all six preference items, qoa, and prqc_4-6; keep raw unchanged

data <- raw[,c("ResponseId", "Sex_birth", "Relationship_status", "preference_imp_health", "preference_imp_kind","preference_imp_physat", "preference_imp_relig","preference_imp_financ","preference_imp_age", "qoa", "prqc_4", "prqc_5", "prqc_6")]

dim(data)
str(data)
```


## 2. Check participant IDs

```{r participant_ids}

#count na
sum(is.na(data$ResponseId))
#count blank
sum(data$ResponseId=="",na.rm=TRUE)

#count duplicates
sum(duplicated(data$ResponseId))

#You can also run this:
summary(data$ResponseId)

#inspect records with missing or blank IDs
missingID<- which(is.na(data$ResponseId))
print(data[missingID,])
#remove the known empty record with no ID, then check the row count
data<-data[!is.na(data$ResponseId),]

```


## 3. Recode sex at birth

```{r sex_at_birth}
# codebook: 0 = Male, 1 = Female, 2 = Intersex
table(data$Sex_birth,useNA="ifany")
#turn Sex_birth into a factor with labels Male, Female, and Intersex
data$Sex_birth<- factor(data$Sex_birth,
                        levels=c(0,1,2),
                        labels= c("Male","Female","Intersex"))

```


## 4. Validate relative preference

```{r preference_vars}
#group all six preference_imp_ variables
prefVars<- c("preference_imp_health", "preference_imp_kind","preference_imp_physat", "preference_imp_relig","preference_imp_financ","preference_imp_age")


#see summary of variables
summary(data[,prefVars])
#count NAs
colSums(is.na(data[,prefVars]))

#calculate total score; leave the total NA if any item is missing
data$prefTotal <- rowSums(data[,prefVars],na.rm = FALSE)
summary(data$prefTotal)

#count those that do not sum to 30 & also not NA
sum(data$prefTotal !=30 & !is.na(data$prefTotal))

#check that each observed allocation is between 0 and 30
data$prefRange <- rowSums(data[,prefVars] <0 | data[,prefVars] >30,
                          na.rm = TRUE) == FALSE


#define prefValid: total present, total equals 30, and each item in range
data$prefValid <- !is.na(data$prefTotal) & data$prefTotal ==30 & data$prefRange
table(data$prefValid)

#make h1Data with ID, Sex_birth, and preference_imp_physat
h1Data <- data[data$prefValid & !is.na(data$Sex_birth), c("ResponseId","Sex_birth","preference_imp_physat")]

dim(h1Data)
head(h1Data)
```


## 5. qoa & commitment
```{r qoa_commitment}
#make relData for respondents currently in a relationship
#include Dating (1), In a committed relationship (2), and Married (3)
table(data$Relationship_status, useNA ="ifany")
relData <- data[data$Relationship_status %in% c(1,2,3),]



#define the items to check; all four use response codes 1-7
#qoa: 1=Strongly disagree, 7=Strongly agree
#prqc_4-6: 1=Not at all, 7=Extremely
likert7 <- c("qoa","prqc_4","prqc_5","prqc_6")

#check the summaries and missing responses
summary(relData[, likert7])
colSums(is.na(relData[, likert7]))

#inspect the response frequencies for each item
for(i in likert7){
  print(i)
  print(table(relData[,i],useNA="ifany"))
}




#replace any codes outside 1-7 with NA
for (i in likert7){
  relData[,i]<- ifelse(relData[,i] %in% 1:7, relData[,i],NA)
}



```

## 6. Calculate commitment

```{r commitment}
#group commitment variables (prqc_4, prqc_5, and prqc_6)
#these ask how committed, dedicated, and devoted respondents are
#none requires reverse coding
comVars <- c("prqc_4","prqc_5","prqc_6")


#calculate commitment as the mean of all three items
#for NAs, conduct available item mean
relData$commitment <- rowMeans(relData[,comVars],na.rm = TRUE)

#check the score
summary(relData$commitment)

#make h2Data with ID, qoa, and commitment
#keep participants with both qoa and commitment present
#do not apply the H1 preference filter to this hypothesis
h2Data <- relData[!is.na(relData$qoa) & !is.na(relData$commitment), c("ResponseId", "qoa", "commitment")]

dim(h2Data)
summary(h2Data)
```

## 7. Check the final tables

```{r final_tables}
#check rows, columns, types, and missing values in h1Data
#one row per participant, one column per variable
dim(h1Data)
str(h1Data)
head(h1Data)
colSums(is.na(h1Data))
table(h1Data$Sex_birth,useNA="ifany")
range(h1Data$preference_imp_physat)
sum(duplicated(h1Data$ResponseId))

#repeat the checks for h2Data; both scores should be within 1-7
dim(h2Data)
str(h2Data)
head(h2Data)
colSums(is.na(h2Data))
range(h2Data$qoa)
range(h2Data$commitment)
sum(duplicated(h2Data$ResponseId))
```

## 8. Add labels and generate codebooks

The descriptions come from the original codebook and our scoring decisions.
`compact_codebook()` adds summaries from the actual data. Knit the Rmd to
display the formatted codebooks.

```{r variable_labels}
#add a description to each h1Data column, in column order
#include the source codes, meaning, and units
var_label(h1Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Sex at birth: original codes 0=Male, 1=Female, 2=Intersex; now stored as a factor",
  "Points allocated to partner physical attractiveness; 0-30 points from a 30-point budget; zero is valid"
)

#add a description to each h2Data column, in column order
#include response anchors and the commitment scoring rule
var_label(h2Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Confidence in finding another appealing partner if the current relationship ended; 1=Strongly disagree, 7=Strongly agree",
  "Relationship commitment: mean of available prqc_4-6 responses, each 1=Not at all to 7=Extremely; no reverse coding; at least one valid response required"
)

```

H1 includes participants with an ID, a valid sex-at-birth category, and six
allocations between 0 and 30 that total 30. Factor level numbers in the
generated table are internal R positions, not the original survey codes.

```{r h1_codebook}
#generate the h1Data codebook
compact_codebook(h1Data)

```

H2 includes participants with an ID, relationship status 1, 2, or 3, and
valid nonmissing qoa and at least one valid commitment response.

```{r h2_codebook}
#generate the h2Data codebook
compact_codebook(h2Data)

```

## 9. Save the final tables

```{r save}
#create data/processed_data if needed
dir.create("data/processed_data",recursive=T,showWarnings=F)

#save h1Data and h2Data without an extra row-number column
write.csv(h1Data,"data/processed_data/practice_h1.csv",row.names=F)
write.csv(h2Data,"data/processed_data/practice_h2.csv",row.names=F)

#read the files back and confirm their dimensions
h1Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h1.csv")
h2Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h2.csv")
dim(h1Saved)
dim(h2Saved)

```
